sentences.text:
THIS CRIMINAL PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

ORDER Petitioners are before this Court calling in question the proceedings in C.C.No.1037/2022 (Crime No.104 of 2021) for the offences punishable under Sections 341, 323, 504, 498A r/w Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2.

During the pendency of the proceedings, the parties to the lis have settled the dispute amongst themselves and have filed an application under Section 320 of the Cr.P.C. seeking permission to compound the offences.

The parties were also before the Family Court, Bengaluru in M.C.No.7186 of 2022 wherein they have filed a Memorandum of Settlement under Section 89 of the CPC r/w Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005 drawing up certain conditions,
one such condition is closure of the present NC: 2023:KHC:21330 proceedings.

The condition insofar as it relates to closure of the present proceedings reads as follows:
"6. The 2nd petitioner agreed to withdraw M.C No 62/2021 pending before Sr. Civil Judge and JMFC, Tarikere.
7.
The 2nd petitioner agreed to co-operate for closure/ quashing of C.C.No.1037/2022 pending before the Addl. Civil Judge and JMFC, Tarikere to dispose off the case at the time of evidence.
8. Both the petitioners state that they have no claims over the movable or immovable properties either existing or to be acquired in future."

3. Since the offences alleged against the petitioners are punishable under Section 498A of the IPC and other offences, which are not against the State or the Society, and in the light of the settlement arrived at between the parties as aforesaid, I deem it appropriate to obliterate the proceedings pending against the petitioners.

4. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) Criminal Petition is disposed.
(ii) Impugned proceedings in C.C.No.1037/2022 pending before the Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, NC: 2023:KHC:21330 Tarikere, Chikkamagaluru stands quashed qua the petitioners.
